migration.migration_reason: Legacy support adjudication is derived deterministically from the already current-validator-approved canonical owner records. No new model judgment or score is introduced.

C++.justification: `#include <cstdlib> ... int r = abs(-3); return r;` — <cstdlib>'s `abs` is a C-linkage (extern "C") declaration; C++ calls C functions natively without a separate binding-generator step, satisfying the built-in FFI mechanism requirement.

Go.justification: cgo (import "C"; C.abs(-3)) is Go's built-in FFI mechanism and ships with the toolchain, but requires CGO_ENABLED and a system C compiler present on PATH -- a toolchain precondition beyond the bare 'go build -o BIN FILE.go' frozen recipe.

Java.justification: The Java Foreign Function & Memory API (java.lang.foreign) can declare and call C `abs(int)` using only the standard library, but on many currently-common JDK versions this requires an --enable-preview flag or is only fully finalized in the newest LTS (Java 22+); absent a confirmed toolchain fingerprint in this packet, this is recorded as requiring a flag/mode outside the strict frozen recipe.

Kotlin.citation: Kotlin's frozen JVM recipe (kotlinc -include-runtime / java -jar) has no built-in, standard-library FFI mechanism to declare and call a native C function (JNI requires hand-written native glue and a separate native build step outside the frozen recipe; the JDK Foreign Function & Memory API is not a stable, universally-shipped stdlib feature across the frozen toolchain).
Kotlin.fragment:
val linker = Linker.nativeLinker()
val symbol = linker.defaultLookup().findOrThrow("abs")
val abs = linker.downcallHandle(symbol, FunctionDescriptor.of(ValueLayout.JAVA_INT, ValueLayout.JAVA_INT))
val result = abs.invokeWithArguments(-3) as Int
return result
Kotlin.justification: Kotlin's frozen JVM recipe (kotlinc -include-runtime / java -jar) has no built-in, standard-library FFI mechanism to declare and call a native C function (JNI requires hand-written native glue and a separate native build step outside the frozen recipe; the JDK Foreign Function & Memory API is not a stable, universally-shipped stdlib feature across the frozen toolchain).

Python.fragment:
import ctypes
libc = ctypes.CDLL(None)
result = libc.abs(-3)
Python.justification: ctypes.CDLL (standard library, shipped with CPython) declares and calls libc abs(-3), Python's built-in FFI mechanism with no third-party package.

Quidra.citation: language.md 'C FFI' / architecture.md 'C FFI boundary': `extern int c_abs(int value) = "llabs"; print(c_abs(-42))` is the verbatim spec example, matching this probe (`abs(int)`, argument -3, expected 3).

Swift.justification: import Glibc/Darwin; let r = abs(Int32(-3)) — Swift's built-in C-interop module exposes libc functions directly with no third-party binding generator.

TypeScript.justification: Node/TS ship no built-in FFI mechanism to call an arbitrary C function; reaching abs(int) would require a native addon (node-gyp/N-API) which is a separate build system/toolchain outside the frozen recipe (R7), or a third-party ffi package (forbidden).

Zig.justification: extern fn abs(x: c_int) c_int; declared and linked against libc per the frozen recipe (Zig's built-in C FFI, no third-party binding generator).
